questions.question: What are the tiny, balloon-like air sacs that make up the structure of the lungs called?
options: Bronchioles
Alveoli
Capillaries
Tracheoles

questions.question: Why are the walls of the alveoli only one cell thick?
options: To allow blood to flow through them directly
To provide a short diffusion distance for gas exchange
To prevent any bacteria from entering the lungs
To keep the lungs lightweight and inflated

questions.question: In which parts of animal, plant, and fungi cells does aerobic cellular respiration take place?
options: Mitochondria and cytoplasm
Nucleus and cell wall
Ribosomes and vacuole
Chloroplasts and cell membrane

questions.question: Why might muscle cells have a significantly higher number of mitochondria compared to skin cells?
options: They need to store more genetic information
They require more energy because they perform a lot of work
They are responsible for absorbing oxygen from the air
They need to produce larger amounts of lactic acid

questions.question: What are the products of anaerobic cellular respiration in microorganisms like yeast?
options: Lactic acid and oxygen
Glucose and water
Carbon dioxide and ethanol
Carbon dioxide and lactic acid

questions.question: What is another term used to describe anaerobic cellular respiration in microorganisms?
options: Photosynthesis
Fermentation
Ventilation
Aeration

questions.question: During vigorous exercise in humans, anaerobic respiration can occur. What waste product is produced that can lead to muscle cramps?
options: Ethanol
Carbon dioxide
Lactic acid
Glucose

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the cellular location of anaerobic cellular respiration?
options: It occurs entirely in the mitochondria and does not use the cytoplasm
It takes place only in the cytoplasm and does not involve the mitochondria
It starts in the chloroplasts and ends in the vacuole
It occurs only inside the nucleus of eukaryotic cells

questions.question: How does the energy release in anaerobic cellular respiration compare to aerobic cellular respiration?
options: It provides more energy and provides it more slowly
It provides less energy and provides it more slowly
It provides more energy and provides it more quickly
It provides less energy, but provides it more quickly

questions.question: Which of the following gases is produced as a waste product during cellular respiration?
options: Oxygen
Carbon dioxide
Nitrogen
Hydrogen

questions.question: Cellular respiration is a chemical process. What fuel, obtained from food, does it use to provide energy for life processes?
options: Carbon dioxide
Protein
Glucose
Oxygen

questions.question: When does cellular respiration happen in living organisms?
options: Only when they are sleeping or resting
Only during the daytime when there is light
All the time in all living organisms to keep them alive
Only when they are actively moving or exercising

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the difference between breathing and respiration?
options: Breathing is a chemical process in cells, while respiration is the physical movement of air
Breathing is the physical movement of air in and out of the lungs, while respiration is a cellular chemical process
Breathing only happens in plants, while respiration only happens in animals
Breathing produces glucose, while respiration produces oxygen

questions.question: What is meant by the term 'vital capacity' of the lungs?
options: The total amount of oxygen that the blood can transport
The volume of air left in the lungs after a normal exhale
The maximum volume of air that can be exhaled after inhaling fully
The speed at which air flows into the lungs during exercise

questions.question: In science, what does it mean if a measurement is said to be accurate?
options: It is expressed to a very large number of decimal places
The measurement is very close to its true value
The measurement was repeated many times with different results
It is an estimated guess made without using any equipment
